_comment: Calibrated 2026-08-27 against the 591-image fixture set in images/ — see research/RESULTS.md, camera-thresholds. Read by BOTH the app camera gate and the server quality gate, at runtime, never bundled. Every number here is answerable: images/check.py measures the set, images/calibrate.py scores these numbers against it. Do not move one without a named fixture and a RESULTS.md row.
_blur: The capture gate measures a 240x180 downscale, which destroys the very defect it is looking for — it flags 23 of 166 known-blurred fixtures, against 152 at full resolution. So this number is an advisory on the phone; the hard reject lives in _enhance_only below.
_fill: fill_fraction_max is deliberately 1.0, i.e. off. The busy box spanning the frame is what a product photograph looks like — at 0.90 this refused 44 of 93 good fixtures as 'too close', including every patterned-background one. Nothing needs it: all 83 too-far fixtures sit at fill 0.11, far below fill_fraction_min.
_camera_only: Below here is the live capture gate only — the server has no preview frames to run these against.
_enhance_only: Server enhancement pipeline only — the app never reads these. Reconciliation §6.
_crop: crop_fill_target is the product's long side as a fraction of the square listing canvas, and it is the only knob — the reconciliation also proposed crop_padding_pct: 8, which is the same number said backwards ((1 - 0.85) / 2 = 7.5% margin per side). Two keys that can disagree about one measurement is a bug waiting to happen, so there is one. Not calibrated against fixtures: 0.85 is the marketplace requirement (spec §9.1), not a measurement of our photographs.
_tiers: Mask confidence and tiers A/B/C. Scored against seg-v1 on 2026-08-28 by research/segmentation/tiers.py: these values catch 5 of the 7 masks a person would refuse to ship, and demote 2 good masks to tier B, which is a safe outcome. A grid search over area/uncertainty/blob values found nothing that does better on this set, so these stay as the reconciliation proposed them — now measured rather than reasoned. What they do NOT catch is in RESULTS.md, and it is a real gap, not a rounding error.
_tone: Contrast and shadow work, product region only. CLAHE runs on the L channel of LAB and nowhere else — on RGB it shifts hue, and a saree changing shade is exactly the misrepresentation the colour lock exists to catch (spec §5.3). The black/white points are percentiles of the product's own lightness, so a dark product is not stretched to look like a bright one. NOT calibrated against fixtures: these are the spec's numbers, and the fixture set has no photograph taken in real artisan light to calibrate them on.
_tone_edge_blur: How far the tone correction fades out across the mask edge, in pixels at the 2000px master. The one tone number that IS measured: BiRefNet's alpha ramps over 3-4px, and on pottery-potter-indoor-04 an 11.1 L correction across that ramp is 3.3 L per pixel, which draws a visible line around the product on tier C. At 4 the ramp is ~11px and the same correction is ~1 L/px. Guarded by test_the_tone_edge_is_not_a_visible_seam, which needs the model and skips without it. Deliberately NOT pipeline.FEATHER_PX: that is tier B's edge treatment and answers a different question.
_white_balance: The stage rule 4 exists to police — the only one that moves colour on purpose. The neutral-pixel path is deliberately NOT gray-world (PIPELINE-RECONCILIATION §5 finding 2 names gray-world as the method that pulls a maroon Sambalpuri toward orange): only the least-chromatic slice votes, so a saree filling the frame gets no vote on its own colour, and a frame with nothing plausibly grey is declined rather than guessed. Measured by images/wb_check.py over 179 fixtures against three synthetic casts — the ground truth is synthetic because images/raw holds no photograph with a recorded illuminant, so this bounds the method's error and does not confirm its accuracy. wb-v1 in images/MANIFEST.md is what would, and it is still empty.
_wb_max_gain_ratio: How far colour may move, as the ratio between the largest and smallest gain. No single value is optimal at every cast strength — the sweep's minimum tracks the cast — so this is chosen on risk, not on the minimum. At 1.3: mean |chroma error| 1.92 vs 7.70 uncorrected on a mild cast, 4.48 vs 15.29 on a medium one, 9.94 vs 20.39 on a strong one, and NO fixture made worse on the medium or strong sets. At 1.6 the medium set is better (2.36) and the mild set puts 30 of 172 fixtures further from the truth than leaving them alone. Rule 1 makes that the wrong trade: under-correcting leaves the photograph closer to as-photographed, over-correcting invents. Re-run: python3 images/wb_check.py --sweep [--cast r,g,b]
_wb_neutral_enabled: OFF, and measured off rather than assumed off. On 33 real photographs from Ekamra Haat with nothing wrong with them, the neutral path damaged 20: every dhokra brass piece lost 43-62% of the product's chroma and a cream pattachitra cloth moved 29.6 degrees of hue. Gold went pewter. No reference-free method can separate warm light from a warm object, and Odisha's crafts are warm. The synthetic sweep in images/wb_check.py could never have found this — every image it scores has been given a cast that wants undoing, so it can only reward correcting. Re-run before changing: python3 images/wb_check.py --control images/haat. Turn this on only with a control run that says it is safe.
_wb_neutral_background_only: Estimate the light from outside the product mask only, so the object being corrected cannot be the thing describing the light. Measured against the frame-wide estimate by images/wb_check.py --control images/haat.
_shadow: Contact shadow, Tier A only. Spec §6.4's numbers, at the 2000px master they were written for: bottom third of the mask, heavy blur, small downward offset, multiplied at low opacity. Tier A only because the shadow is drawn from the mask's own outline, so a mask we do not trust would draw a shadow we cannot trust either — and Tier C keeps the real background, which already has the real shadow. NOT calibrated against fixtures: nothing in images/ has a known-correct shadow to score against, so these are the spec's numbers and an eye. The one hard constraint is measured and tested: the listing's corners must stay exactly 255,255,255, because marketplaces reject near-white.
_shadow_squash: How flat the shadow lies, as a fraction of the height of the mask's bottom third. The spec's recipe has no squash and draws the shadow behind the product, where the (1 - mask) term that protects the product deletes nearly all of it — the result is a fringe invisible at listing size. Flattening it toward the contact line is what puts it on the ground, under the object, where it can be seen.
_sharpen: Mild unsharp mask on the L channel only, product region only. Spec §5.5: no sharpening beyond a mild unsharp mask, and no denoise strong enough to smooth weave texture — so the denoise half is not built at all, because a weave IS high-frequency detail and no denoiser can tell it from grain. sharpen_max_overshoot is the ceiling PIPELINE-RECONCILIATION §2 asked for: an unsharp mask brightens one side of an edge and darkens the other, and past a few L units that stops being contrast and becomes a halo, which is detail the photograph does not contain. The amount tapers to zero as the product's own sharpness approaches sharpen_skip_above, because sharpening an already-crisp photograph only adds halos. NOT calibrated: nothing in images/ has a known-correct sharpening to score against.
_sharpen_skip_above: On the RATIO of Laplacian variance before and after a 1px blur, not on the variance itself. The variance alone measures how patterned the subject is: across haat-v1's textiles it spans 176 to 10819, a 60x range set by the weave and not the lens, so using it would sharpen plain products hard and refuse busy ones. The ratio divides the subject out — medians across brass, dhokra and textile go from 262/586/1061 to 5.9/6.9/5.7. At 12 the two visibly crispest photographs in the set decline and everything else gets a mild amount.
